FailList.Trigger: An Evaluation grader crashes or is contaminated. Or the operator, who holds the unblinding map, runs more than one grading for a subject, or re-evaluates an unchanged policy/build after a failing lock.
FailList.Problem: The plan claims one blind grading session, but §20.1 refuses a different capture only after a lock. So several captures per materialization are accepted before the lock, and LockBlindGrades/AttestReview pick one by artifact ID. Nothing limits materializations or locks per Evaluation SubjectDigest. AttestReview does not require its receipt to be the locked capture. §20.2 accepts any matching AGREE even when another lock for the same policy/build failed. §18's paired-case rerun remedy does not fit §19.1's single session that grades all runs, so a grading failure has no defined retry.
FailList.Consequence: Undisclosed selection among gradings or evaluations can flip the aggregate that gates activation. How grader failures are handled is left to operators and implementers, which contradicts 'no selective retry'.
FailList.RequiredResolution: (1) Per workspace and Evaluation SubjectDigest, allow GradingAttempt 0, and attempt 1 only after attempt 0 is server-recorded as GradingInvalid. Each attempt uses a new review workspace with exactly one Ready materialization, exactly one server-minted MCP session since Ready, and at most one capture. Another session or a distinct capture is refused with 409 review_capture_invalid and records GradingInvalid. (2) GradingInvalid means: CLI failure; not exactly one final response; a missing or non-Disabled ledger entry; a context/projection mismatch; a refused capture; or a 400 from LockBlindGrades. A regrade reuses the same immutable results with no behavioral rerun, replacing §18's paired-rerun remedy for grading-only failures. A second GradingInvalid blocks activation. (3) Allow at most one EngineeringEvaluationGradeLock per SubjectDigest. Evaluation AttestReview requires its receipt artifact to equal the lock's CapturedResponseArtifactId. (4) EvalAggregate infrastructure accounting lists every attempt, session and capture. (5) §20.2 also refuses when, for the same workspace, policySha256 and buildArtifactSha256, any lock has a failing threshold verdict, or a frozen protocol has no lock and no operator-signed abandonment audit (PolicyAudit Kind EvaluationAbandoned, shown in status diagnostics). (6) Add tests for each rule.

FailList.Trigger: A staging or production instance restarts with a new build or policy hash and no matching attestation, or reconciliation has to evaluate buildArtifactSha256.
FailList.Problem: (a) The plan holds the workspace inactive 'before allowing gated BDP work' but never says what the completion and TODO gates do during the hold. Three readings are possible: keep enforcing, refuse gated targets, or fall back to base rules. There is no applicability branch, item or remedy for it, and returning a 409 from a completion endpoint would violate §14.1. (b) buildArtifactSha256 and the 'operator-approved build artifact manifest' are not defined anywhere else. Undefined: whether it covers the server only or the server plus nine plugins; who produces it; its canonical form; how it is carried, given the signed payload has no field for it; and how both the server and the harness compute the same value.
FailList.Consequence: An implementation can either silently drop enforcement after an unevaluated deployment, or block completions with an error outside the contract. The build binding may end up trivial or impossible to match. Whether every server patch needs a new 72-run evaluation is left undecided.
FailList.RequiredResolution: (a) Define HeldInactive. Committed settings stay unchanged. For every Agent target that §13.3 rules 5-6 would gate, the completion gate and EngineeringTodoExitPolicy refuse through their normal HTTP 400 contracts, with item engineeringPolicy and a new remedy obtain_activation_evaluation. Add that remedy to the remedy list, the C8 golden contract and the Get-CloseRemedy fixtures; the drain treats it like other engineering items. Unchanged: base-only targets, failed/canceled targets, trusted origins, guidance delivery, evidence create/run/read, status and admin recovery. Status adds activationState Active|Dormant|HeldInactive with the diagnostic. No 409 leaves a completion endpoint. (b) Define BuildArtifactManifest v1 as canonical {schemaVersion:1, releaseVersion, serverPackageSha256, plugins:[{id, version, packageSha256}]}, covering all nine plugins sorted by id. buildArtifactSha256 is the SHA-256 of those canonical bytes. BuildTooling's release build emits the manifest, and the signed change-manifest payload gains buildArtifactSha256. UpdateService checks the installed server package against serverPackageSha256 and installs the manifest beside the binary. Reconciliation requires manifest digest = signed value = attested value; otherwise it refuses or holds the workspace inactive. The harness records the same digest. Plugin entries are enforced only by the release checklist. Add tests.

FailList.Trigger: Behavioral runs execute on isolated evaluation instances, while results, grading, the lock and attestation have to live in each activated workspace's own store. Production, or another BDPv4 workspace, is activated after staging.
FailList.Problem: (a) RecordResults references raw observations only as existing artifact IDs and must validate 'all retained ledger/results'. But the run ledgers are plugin-local on other instances, imports are inert, and only review captures create DeliveryLedger/HvReceipt artifacts. So the per-prompt validity check in §15.5 can only rest on harness-authored JSON. This is the R9-01 gap for behavioral runs; it was latent and I missed it earlier. (b) §13.5 runs one evaluation before staging and lets it gate staging and production. But attestations and locks are workspace-scoped, the protocol must be frozen in the same store before runs, and nothing transfers evidence between stores.
FailList.Consequence: The server-side contamination check is not implementable as written. Production activation will need a new evaluation that the plan does not schedule.
FailList.RequiredResolution: (a) Each RecordResults run entry carries exact capture bytes: {cliResultUtf8Base64, sessionExportUtf8Base64, deliveryLedgerUtf8Base64, launch, evaluationInstanceId}. They go through §20.1's parsing, limits, credential refusal and errors, and are stored as HvReceipt/DeliveryLedger artifacts referenced by observableArtifactIds. The server validates the ledger state of every ingress and tool-loop dispatch against §15.5 and refuses with 409 review_capture_invalid. State explicitly that binding these artifacts to the isolated instance's minted turns is operator-attested. (b) FreezeProtocol carries targetWorkspaceIds. Runs start only after every target store holds the identical protocol hash. Each target then records, grades once (per R10-01), locks and attests on its own. A target without a pre-run freeze needs a new evaluation. Amend §13.5 to match. Add tests.
